newsitem.title: CANADA: Ballots going out for Canada barley monopoly vote.
newsitem.headline: Ballots going out for Canada barley monopoly vote.

text.p: Around 76,000 ballots were being sent out to barley growers across the Canadian Prairies on Thursday for a vote on the Canadian Wheat Board's export monopoly, the plebiscite's administrator said.
Craig Fossay, partner of KPMG, the chartered accountants chosen to administer the vote, said farmers had to return the ballots by February 28.

Farmers are being asked to decide to choose between exporting feed and malt barley through private exporters or retaining the status quo. Currently all barley is exported through the CWB but domestic feed sales are handled privately.

About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported and the balance fed to livestock or brewed in Canada. Western Canada produced around 15 million tonnes of barley in 1996, according to private trade estimates.
